pairs: Si quis furatus fuerit bovem aut ovem,
“If anyone will have stolen an ox or a sheep,
and if he kills it or sells it,
quinque boves pro uno bove restituet,
then he will restore five oxen for one ox,
et quatuor oves pro una ove.
and four sheep for one sheep.
Si effringens fur domum sive suffodiens fuerit inventus,
If a thief will have been discovered breaking into a house, or digging under it,
and he has received a mortal wound,
he who struck him down will not be guilty of blood.
Quod si orto sole hoc fecerit,
But if he did this when the sun was risen,
Si non habuerit quod pro furto reddat,
If he does not have the means to make restitution for the theft,
Si inventum fuerit apud eum quod furatus est,
If whatever he stole should be found with him,
Si læserit quispiam agrum vel vineam,
If there is any damage to a field or a vineyard,
et dimiserit jumentum suum ut depascatur aliena:
when he has released his cattle to pasture on the land of a stranger,
quidquid optimum habuerit in agro suo,
he shall repay the best of what he has in his own field,
according to the estimation of the damage.
If a fire will have been discovered departing from brush,
and taking hold in stacks of grain,
or in crops standing in the fields,
whoever ignited the fire shall repay the damages.
Si quis commendaverit amico pecuniam aut vas in custodiam,
If anyone will have entrusted money,
and if these have been stolen from the one who received them:
dominus domus applicabitur ad deos, et jurabit quod non extenderit manum in rem proximi sui,
the lord of the house will be brought before the heavens to swear that he did not lay his hand on the goods of his neighbor,
so as to perpetrate any fraud,
tam in bove quam in asino,
such as with an ox, or a donkey,
nor to do anything that would be able to cause damage.
The case of both shall be brought before the heavens.
And if they give judgment against him,
he shall repay double to his neighbor.
Si quis commendaverit proximo suo asinum,
If anyone will have entrusted a donkey,
or any animal to the keeping of his neighbor,
or have been captured by enemies,
then there shall be an oath between them,
quod non extenderit manum ad rem proximi sui:
that he did not lay his hand on the goods of his neighbor.
And the owner shall accept the oath,
and he will not be compelled to make restitution.
But if it will have been taken away by theft,
he shall repay the damages to the owner.
If it has been eaten by a wild beast,
deferat ad eum quod occisum est,
let him carry what was killed to him,
and then he shall not make restitution.
Qui a proximo suo quidquam horum mutuo postulaverit,
If anyone borrows from his neighbor any of these things,
et debilitatum aut mortuum fuerit domino non præsente,
and it has died or been disabled when the owner was not present,
he shall be compelled to make restitution.
But if the owner was present,
maxime si conductum venerat pro mercede operis sui.
especially if it had been brought for hired work.
Si seduxerit quis virginem necdum desponsatam,
If a man has led astray a virgin not yet betrothed,
and he has slept with her,
and have her as a wife.
If the father of the virgin is not willing to give her,
he shall pay money according to manner of a dowry,
which virgins are accustomed to receive.
You shall not permit practitioners of the black arts to live.
Qui coierit cum jumento, morte moriatur.
Whoever has sexual intercourse with an animal shall be put to death.
You shall not harass the newcomer,
advenæ enim et ipsi fuistis in terra Ægypti.
For you yourselves were once newcomers in the land of Egypt.
You shall not harm a widow or an orphan.
they will cry out to me,
and I will hear their cry.
And my fury will be enraged,
and I will strike you down with the sword.
And your wives will become widows,
and your sons will become orphans.
Si pecuniam mutuam dederis populo meo pauperi qui habitat tecum,
If you lend money to the poor of my people who live among you,
you shall not coerce them like a collector,
Si pignus a proximo tuo acceperis vestimentum,
If you take a garment from your neighbor as a pledge,
you shall return it to him again before the setting of the sun.
Ipsum enim est solum, quo operitur,
For it is all that he has to cover himself,
indumentum carnis ejus, nec habet aliud in quo dormiat:
to clothe his body; nor does he have anything else in which to sleep.
If he cries out to me,
You shall not disparage the heavens,
et principi populi tui non maledices.
and you shall not speak evil of the leader of your people.
Decimas tuas et primitias tuas non tardabis reddere:
You shall not delay in paying your tithes and your first-fruits.
You shall give the firstborn of your sons to me.
You shall do likewise with those of the oxen and the sheep.
septem diebus sit cum matre sua,
let it be with its mother;
on the eighth day you shall repay it to me.
You shall be holy men for me.
from which beasts will have tasted,
but you will throw it to the dogs.”
